inputs: Messages of 0, 1, 15, 16 and 17 bytes padded with PKCS#7 and a 16-byte block
expected: Padded lengths are 16, 16, 16, 32 and 32; final bytes are 10, 0f, 01, 10 and 0f
limitations: One fixed block size and five lengths; not an exhaustive length matrix.

inputs: Round-trip padding for lengths 0 through 32, plus empty, non-multiple, zero-length, oversized and inconsistent padding
expected: Every round trip returns the original message; every malformed padding is rejected
limitations: Strict-removal checks on fixed malformed cases; not a fuzzing campaign.

inputs: 15-byte and 16-byte plaintexts padded and encrypted with AES-128-CBC without automatic padding
expected: 15 bytes produce a 16-byte ciphertext; 16 bytes produce a 32-byte ciphertext; both decrypt and unpad correctly
limitations: One key, IV and two lengths; it demonstrates overhead, not protocol behavior.

inputs: A fixed two-block AES-128-CBC ciphertext and a simulated valid-padding oracle
expected: The oracle rejects the original ciphertext, and the byte-flipping search recovers the original last plaintext byte 60
limitations: One fixed byte and fixed ciphertext; not a full multi-byte or end-to-end protocol attack.
